chunks: And from him, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Dawood ibn Farqad, from al-Mualla ibn Khunays who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): When there comes a hadith from your first ones and a hadith from your last ones, by which of the two should we act? So he said: Adhere to it until there reaches you from the living one; then if there does reach you from the living one, take his words.
He (the narrator) said: Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: We, by God, do not lead you into anything except what is within your capacity.
And in another report: Take the most recent.

key_terms.الْحَيّ: The living one — referring to the current/living Imam who is the supreme authority for present guidance
key_terms.بِالْأَحْدَثِ: The most recent — in case of conflicting narrations, the later one reflects more updated guidance
key_terms.يَسَعُكُمْ: What is within your capacity — the Imam assures followers that his guidance does not impose undue hardship

ai.seo_question: How should conflicting hadiths from different Imams be resolved according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Al-Mualla ibn Khunays, a companion of Imam al-Sadiq, asked him how to resolve conflicting narrations from earlier and later Imams. The Imam's response establishes a key hermeneutical principle: the narration from the living (current) Imam takes precedence, and in another version of the same ruling, take the more recent narration. This hadith is foundational in Shia usul al-fiqh for resolving contradictions in the hadith corpus, with the living Imam representing the authoritative and updated source of guidance for contemporary believers.
